fable.rjd3

fable.rjd3 brings the seasonal adjustment algorithms of JDemetra+ v3 to the fable framework. It lets you seasonally adjust tsibble series with the standard model() / components() workflow, on one or many series at once, and gives access to everything JDemetra+ computes.

  • Four models: X13() (X-13ARIMA), TRAMOSEATS() (TRAMO-SEATS), and the pre-adjustment models REGARIMA() and TRAMO().
  • Full control of the specification, either with the specification objects of the rjd3* packages or with specials in the model formula, including regressors taken from the columns of the tsibble.
  • Standard verbs: components(), forecast(), glance(), tidy(), report(), fitted(), residuals(), augment(), outliers(), refit(), stream(), and backcast().
  • Any JDemetra+ indicator with jd3_indicator(), from the Java result kept in the model.
  • JDemetra+ workspaces: import_jws() and export_jws().

Installation

fable.rjd3 is built on the JDemetra+ v3 R packages (rjd3toolkit, rjd3x13, rjd3tramoseats and rjd3workspace), which requires Java 21 or higher.

To install the developpment version:

  • From r-universe:
install.packages("fable.rjd3", repos = c("https://aqlt.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
  • From GitHub:
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("AQLT/fable.rjd3")

Example

The series must be a regular, univariate tsibble with a yearmonth or yearquarter index. Monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, four-monthly and semi-annual series are supported: the frequency is deduced from the interval between observations (for example, a yearmonth index with a step of 6 months is a semi-annual series).

library(fable.rjd3)

air <- as_tsibble(AirPassengers)

mb <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(value),
    ts  = TRAMOSEATS(value)
)
mb
#> # A mable: 1 x 2
#>                                x13                                 ts
#>                            <model>                            <model>
#> 1 <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)> <TRAMO-SEATS, ARIMA(0,1,0)(0,1,1)>

components() returns the decomposition as a dable (trend, seasonal, irregular and seasonally adjusted series):

components(mb)
#> # A dable: 288 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [2]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112  122.    0.920     0.996          122.
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118  124.    0.948     1.00           125.
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132  126.    1.05      0.994          125.
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129  128.    1.00      1.01           129.
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121  128.    0.939     1.01           129.
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135  127.    1.07      0.998          127.
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148  126.    1.19      0.988          125.
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148  126.    1.17      0.999          126.
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136  127.    1.07      1.00           128.
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119  128.    0.925     1.00           129.
#> # ℹ 278 more rows
library(ggtime)
ggplot2::autoplot(components(mb))

Specification

The specification is set with the spec argument, or with specials in the formula:

mb_log <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(
        value ~ transform(fun = "Log") +
            outlier(outliers.type = c("AO", "LS")),
        spec = "rsa3"
    )
)

Forecasts

The forecasts of the raw series come from the pre-adjustment model, as distributions:

forecast(mb, h = 12)
#> # A fable: 24 x 4 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [2]
#>    .model    index
#>    <chr>     <mth>
#>  1 x13    1961 Jan
#>  2 x13    1961 Feb
#>  3 x13    1961 Mar
#>  4 x13    1961 Apr
#>  5 x13    1961 May
#>  6 x13    1961 Jun
#>  7 x13    1961 Jul
#>  8 x13    1961 Aug
#>  9 x13    1961 Sep
#> 10 x13    1961 Oct
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: value <dist>, .mean <dbl>

Updating a model 

air_old <- air[air$index < yearmonth("1960 Jan"), ]
air_new <- air[air$index >= yearmonth("1960 Jan"), ]

mb_old <- model(air_old, x13 = X13(value))
mb_new <- stream(mb_old, air_new)   # refresh policy "Fixed" by default

JDemetra+ workspaces 

mb <- import_jws("path/to/workspace.xml")   # keys: `sap` and `series`
export_jws(mb, "path/to/new_workspace.xml")
